keyword: how do astronauts go to the bathroom

verifications.claim: Astronauts use the Universal Waste Management System (UWMS).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: NASA is launching a new space toilet, the Universal Waste Management System (UWMS), to the International Space Station (R4); The space agency’s Universal Waste Management System (UWMS) (R5); The important components of the Universal Waste Management System (UWMS) space toilet (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Directly named and described as the system astronauts use in multiple sources.

verifications.claim: The Universal Waste Management System (UWMS) uses airflow instead of water to pull waste away from the body in microgravity.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: In the absence of gravity, space toilets use air flow to pull urine and feces away from the body and into the proper receptacles (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly states airflow pulls waste away in microgravity.

verifications.claim: The Universal Waste Management System (UWMS) uses a funnel for urine.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: The crew use a specially shaped funnel and hose for urine (R4); urine-collection devices that work for both male and female astronauts (R5); elongated and scooped-out funnels that allow astronauts to urinate (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Directly mentions funnel for urine collection in UWMS.

verifications.claim: The Universal Waste Management System (UWMS) uses a small seat for solids.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: a small raised toilet seat for pooping (R2); a small raised toilet seat for pooping (R3); the seat for bowel movements. The UWMS seat may look uncomfortably small (R4); small toilet (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources describe small seat for solids/pooping in new toilet/UWMS.

verifications.claim: The funnel is equipped with suction to manage waste.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: While urinating, astronauts hold a suction funnel to their skin to prevent leaks (R7)
verifications.reasoning: R7 explicitly calls it a suction funnel; others imply via system airflow.

verifications.claim: The small seat is equipped with suction to manage waste.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: this toilet starts suctioning as soon as the lid is lifted (R2); A new feature of the UWMS is the automatic start of air flow when the toilet lid is lifted (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Suction/airflow activates for seat to manage waste.

verifications.claim: Fans create suction when the toilet lid is lifted.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: this toilet starts suctioning as soon as the lid is lifted (R2); automatic start of air flow when the toilet lid is lifted (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources mention suction/airflow starts on lid lift, fans implied but not explicitly stated.

verifications.claim: The suction prevents waste from floating away.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: to prevent things from drifting away (R2); to prevent things from drifting away (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated purpose of suction.

verifications.claim: The suction controls odors.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: to control the stink (R2); which also helps with odor control (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly mentioned for odor control.

verifications.claim: Astronauts use foot restraints to stay in place.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: The UWMS includes foot restraints and handholds for astronauts to keep themselves from floating away (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Directly states foot restraints in UWMS.

verifications.claim: Astronauts use toe bars to stay in place.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.evidence: No relevant content found
verifications.reasoning: No mention of toe bars in any source.

verifications.claim: Astronauts use thigh straps to stay in place.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: astronauts used thigh straps (original toilet) (R2); consistent astronaut feedback indicated that the traditional thigh straps were a hassle (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Thigh straps used in older toilets, not new UWMS; new uses foot restraints/handholds.

verifications.claim: The toilet seat is smaller than on Earth to ensure a tight seal.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: the toilet seat is smaller than the one in your house. To make sure there’s a tight fit (R2); small toilet and to keep a tight seal (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly smaller for tight seal/fit.

verifications.claim: A funnel connected to a hose collects urine.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: a hose with a funnel at the end for peeing (R2); hose with a funnel at the end for peeing (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Direct description.

verifications.claim: Urine is sent to a recycling system (UPA).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: feeds pre-treated urine into a regenerative system (R4); Urine Processor Assembly (UPA) (R7)
verifications.reasoning: UPA explicitly named as urine recycling system.

verifications.claim: The UPA turns urine into drinking water.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Urine Processor Assembly (UPA), Water Recovery System... turns it into drinkable water (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Directly states UPA processes urine to drinkable water.

verifications.claim: Feces are collected in special bags.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Poop is vacuumed into garbage bags (R2); Solid waste in individual water-tight bags (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Consistently described as bags for feces.

verifications.claim: Special bags are compressed and stored in sealed containers.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Solid waste in individual water-tight bags is compacted in a removable fecal storage canister (R4); put into airtight containers (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Bags compacted/stored in sealed containers.

verifications.claim: Sealed containers are eventually removed and disposed of after the mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: The containers are then loaded into a cargo ship... burns up on re-entry (R4); loaded into a cargo ship that brought supplies... burns up (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Containers disposed via cargo ships post-mission/use.

verifications.claim: The toilet is located in a small, private compartment (the Waste and Hygiene Compartment) on the International Space Station.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.evidence: No relevant content found
verifications.reasoning: No source mentions 'Waste and Hygiene Compartment'; locations like Tranquility noted but not this name.

verifications.claim: The newest NASA toilet is used on the ISS.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: to the International Space Station (R4); sent to the International Space Station (R5); sent to the ISS in 2020 (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly installed on ISS.

verifications.claim: The newest NASA toilet is used for Artemis missions.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: installed in Orion for the Artemis II (R4); installed in the Orion capsule for Artemis II (R5); fitted into the Orion space capsule, the crew vehicle of the Artemis mission (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Directly for Artemis.

verifications.claim: The newest NASA toilet is more compact than older models.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: 65% smaller and 40% lighter build than the current space station toilet (R4); half the size of the Russian-constructed toilets (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly smaller/compact.

verifications.claim: The newest NASA toilet is designed for better comfort and efficiency.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Offers More Comfort, Improved Efficiency (title R4); more comfortable, easier to use (R5); taking astronaut feedback about existing facilities into account (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated in titles and text.

verifications.claim: The newest NASA toilet accommodates both male and female crew members more easily than older models.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: easier to use for both men and women (R2); The funnel and seat can be used simultaneously, reflecting feedback from female astronauts (R4); urine-collection devices that work for both male and female astronauts (R5); better suited to women (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Designed unisex, improved for women over prior male-focused designs.
